title: The string library
description:
Write in `solution.c`, using `string.h`, `ctype.h` and `stdio.h` where they help:

```c
int count_words(const char *s);                       /* words are runs of non-space characters (isspace) */
int starts_with(const char *s, const char *prefix);   /* 1 or 0 */
void format_name(char *out, size_t size, const char *first, const char *last);
                                                      /* "Lovelace, Ada" - never more than size bytes */
int parse_number(const char *s, long *result);        /* 1 and *result set if s is a whole number
                                                         (spaces around it are fine), otherwise 0 */
```

`long *result` is a pointer (lesson 3.03): the function stores the number with `*result = value;`.
hints: For `parse_number`, `strtol(s, &end, 10)` sets `end` just past the number. If `end == s` nothing was read; afterwards skip spaces with `isspace` and check you reached the `'\0'`.
